conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice. Domains are nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open subsets of R^d, d ∈ {2,3}. Pressure space Q=L²₀(D) consists of real L² classes with spatial integral zero and carries the L² norm.
A pressure sensor is a bounded real-linear functional on Q; its norm is sup{|S(q)|: ||q||₂≤1}. Sensor vectors carry the Euclidean norm.
V=H¹₀(D;R^d) carries the gradient norm. The weak viscous form is 2ν∫ε(u):ε(v), the pressure term is −∫p div(v), ν>0, and div(B_D q)=q with ||∇B_D q||₂≤C_div(D)||q||₂.
Normalized pressures q belong to Q; unnormalized representatives p belong to real L²(D). Gauge invariance of an unnormalized weighted reading means invariance under every real constant shift p↦p+c.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice, d∈{2,3}, D nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open, and ν>0. With V=H¹₀(D;R^d) in the gradient norm and Q=L²₀(D), let (u_F,p_F) be the unique weak Stokes pair for F∈V'. For a positive integer m and bounded sensors S₁,…,S_m∈Q', define O(F)=(S₁(p_F),…,S_m(p_F)). Then F↦p_F and O are real-linear, and for every F,G∈V', ||O(F)−O(G)||₂≤3C_div(D)(Σ_j||S_j||²)^(1/2)||F−G||_{V'}, where C_div(D) is a finite divergence-right-inverse bound.

Assume Countable Choice. For d∈{2,3} and nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open D⊂R^d, set Q=L²₀(D) with the L² norm. A bounded Stokes pressure sensor is a bounded real-linear functional S:Q→R, with operator norm sup_{||q||₂≤1}|S(q)|. Its reading at normalized pressure q is S(q).

Assume Countable Choice. For d∈{2,3}, nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz open D, V=H¹₀(D;R^d), Q=L²₀(D), and real g∈L²(D), S_g(q)=∫gq is a bounded pressure sensor. Writing ḡ=|D|⁻¹∫g, one has S_g=S_{g−ḡ} on Q. For p∈L²(D), the weak pressure term −∫p div(v) is unchanged by every constant shift for v∈V. The unnormalized reading ∫gp is invariant under every constant shift if and only if ∫g=0, equivalently g∈Q.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact domain class, H¹₀ closure convention, velocity gradient norm, real mean-zero pressure space, symmetric gradient, and signs of the weak Stokes forms.
Existence of a bounded linear divergence right inverse on the stated Lipschitz domains under Countable Choice, with finite mesh-independent C_div(D).

Unique normalized weak Stokes solutions for all loads in V' and the exact pressure estimate ||p||₂≤3C_div(D)||F||_{V'}. Its forms, norms, domain assumptions, viscosity assumption, and choice hypothesis match the assigned consumers.
For zero-boundary H¹ vector fields, divergence belongs to L² and has integral zero; this establishes invariance of the weak pressure term under constant shifts.
Integrability and boundedness of weighted pressure pairings, finiteness of spatial means, and continuity estimates for the gradient-forcing example.

seams_checked.note: The actual use is pthm-fd-creeping-lipschitz-pressure invoking thm-fd-stokes-load-observable-stability. The consumer preserves Countable Choice, the bounded connected Lipschitz domain, positive viscosity, gradient-norm velocity space, mean-zero pressure, bounded real-linear sensors, Euclidean output norm, and 3C_div constant. Its L² body-force loads are shown bounded using Poincare, and the physical output estimate multiplies the mathematical bound by ρ₀U₀². Conversely, the supplier requires no physical premises and promises neither finite-Reynolds approximation accuracy nor empirical validation; the consumer retains these limitations.
